title: Client offline recovery lanes — sketch
content:
Context:
- we need a robust, client-forward pattern for recovering LLM sessions when devices go offline, or network drops, or the client intentionally suspends. existing sketches cover prefetch + snapshotting; this doc explores explicit \"lanes\" for resuming with graded guarantees and an associated minimal API.

Goal:
- define API / config shape that clients (mobile/desktop/edge) can implement to provide fast UX while keeping server cost predictable.
- clarify server-side state transitions and SLA expectations for each lane.
- enumerate heuristics for accepting a resume, merging KV-cache, and fallback policies if state diverges.

High-level idea: \"Recovery lanes\" = a set of semantics a client can request when resuming a session. Lanes trade latency vs. consistency vs. cost. Server responds with accepted lane + required replay steps.

Lanes (initial proposal):
1) immediate-hot (best-effort merge)
  - semantics: server attempts a light-weight delta-merge with KV-prefix and grants instant continuation. May accept stale cache.
  - SLO: <75ms added latency on resume path if KG size small; best-effort correctness.
  - use-case: chat UI reconnect, user expects minimal disruption.

2) validated-warm (validate checkpoints)
  - semantics: server verifies checkpoint hash + applies incremental replay (recompute few tokens) before allowing generation.
  - SLO: ~200-800ms depending on replay length.
  - use-case: continuity with moderate safety; good for short-sessions where correctness matters.

3) authoritative-cold (reconstruct)
  - semantics: server reconstructs full canonical context from persisted conversation + replays to rebuild cache. Reserved for long idle time or suspected divergence.
  - SLO: variable; background prioritized, may return streaming rehydrate progress.
  - use-case: enterprise audits, long-running contexts, debugging.

API shape (sketch):
- ResumeSessionRequest {
    session_id: string,
    lane_hint: \"immediate-hot\" | \"validated-warm\" | \"authoritative-cold\",
    client_checkpoint_hash?: string,
    last_seen_token_index?: number,
    client_kv_manifest?: [ { key: string, hash: string, size: number } ],
    prefer_streaming_rehydrate?: boolean
  }

- ResumeSessionResponse {
    accepted_lane: string,
    server_checkpoint_hash?: string,
    required_replay_from_token_index?: number,
    merge_strategy: \"fast-merge\" | \"validate-then-merge\" | \"rebuild\",
    delta_actions?: [ string ], // short list of actions server will take before generation allowed
    estimated_warmup_ms: number,
    resume_token: string // single-use token to continue generation requests
  }

Notes on shapes: keep fields minimal so mobile SDKs can implement. client_kv_manifest reduces handshake size vs full blob upload. server returns resume_token to bind the resume attempt to a particular warm-up operation (prevents race).

State transitions (server-side):
- sessions store: { session_id, canonical_conversation_ref, latest_checkpoint_hash, last_active_at, kv_index_manifest }
- on ResumeSessionRequest:
  1) quick-check heuristics: if last_active_at < cold_threshold => accepted_lane->authoritative-cold
  2) if checkpoint_hash matches latest and lane_hint == immediate-hot => accept immediate-hot with fast-merge
  3) if mismatch + lane_hint==immediate-hot => server may respond with accepted_lane=validated-warm and required_replay_from_token_index = X
  4) server persists a resume_token and attaches a short TTL (e.g., 30s)

Merge strategies:
- fast-merge: assume client's KV keys are mostly compatible. server will overlay client keys onto server cache with LRU heuristics. if key->value hash conflict, prefer server canonical unless client reports more recent write_ts.
- validate-then-merge: server replays small tail of tokens (N=8-32) to see if model outputs drift; if drift, fallback to rebuild.
- rebuild: fetch canonical history from DB, replay entire conversation to rebuild KV.

Protocol diagram (ASCII):
Client -> ResumeSessionRequest(lane_hint=immediate-hot, client_ck=abc) -> Server
Server -> quick-check -> decide accepted_lane
if accepted_lane==immediate-hot -> return resume_token + estimated_warmup_ms=15 -> Client uses resume_token to send GenerationRequest
if accepted_lane==validated-warm -> server does small replay (async sync), returns required_replay_from_token_index and resume_token -> client optionally waits
if authoritative-cold -> server streams rehydrate logs and progress, client shows spinner

Edge cases / Race conditions:
- multiple clients concurrently resuming same session: resume_token single-use reduces conflicts; additional concurrency control: small mutex on session warmup path, queue and emit backpressure signal to clients.
- client lying about checkpoint_hash (malicious or bug): server always validates critical hashes before accepting authoritative operations.
- KV growth attack: limit manifest size + require server-side gating for very large manifests.

Cost model notes:
- immediate-hot is cheap (mostly a few KV lookups). validated-warm costs replay compute. authoritative-cold costs full replay compute.
- we should expose per-lane cost multipliers in billing (or keep internal for now). tag in console: resume.path.cost_multiplier

Telemetry/observability:
- instrument: resume_lane_requested, resume_lane_accepted, resume_warmup_ms, resume_replay_token_count, resume_conflict_detected.
- surface in console per-session timelines + per-route resume rate.

SDK ergonomics (mobile):
- keep resume flow in SDK method: Session.resume(lane_hint, onProgress, onReady) -> abstracts polling and streaming.
- store minimal client_checkpoint_hash computed from last N messages + metadata.
- backoff heuristics for repeated resume failures: exponential backoff + degrade to authoritative-cold after N failures.

Open questions / TODOs (brain dump):
- What is the canonical checkpoint hash algorithm? (rolling hash over token ids + metadata?) Need stable across tokenizer changes.
- How to support partial KV eviction on client vs server? If client has partial cache, merge heuristics need to be conservative.
- Should we allow server to request an immediate client upload of specific KV blobs when fast-merge fails (pull-on-demand)?
- Telemetry: add synthetic resume tests in staging to measure tail latencies and frequency.
- Security: ensure resume_token cannot be used to escalate privileges; map resume_token to session ACL.

Experiments to run:
- A/B: accept immediate-hot aggressively vs conservative (fall back to validated-warm) and measure user perceived reconnection time vs error rate.
- Replay N tuning: measure drift detection vs cost for N in [4,8,16,32].
- Manifest compression: test using bloom filter + small hash list to reduce handshake size.

Next steps:
- sync with SDK owners (Jonah) to align resume_token TTL and SDK APIs.
- write small PoC server handler to implement quick-check heuristics + resume_token lifecycle (LR-4821).
- add telemetry counters and synthetic test to staging.

Notes to self: keep this lean. avoid overfitting to mobile only—desktop and edge clients will benefit. draft a short ADR if core semantics are stable.

References / links in-text: see linked_artifacts above.
